title: Keyboard Manager remappings are ignored in Windows Terminal

judgment.rationale: The issue supplies an exact Caps Lock-to-Esc remap and the Windows Terminal/PowerShell/WSL versions, but does not establish whether Terminal is elevated or whether the same remap works in another app. Those facts distinguish an OS integrity-level input-injection boundary from a Terminal-specific path before a code fix is justified.
evidence: PowerToys 0.102.2814; remap Caps Lock to Esc; failure occurs in Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 running PowerShell 7.4.6 or WSL2 2.7.3.0 with Ubuntu 24.04.5.
The live body does not state whether PowerToys or Terminal is elevated and does not report a same-session comparison in Notepad or another ordinary app.
The sole live comment is automated triage at 2026-10-14T14:17:09Z, which cites #28728 as a possible duplicate, not a confirmed duplicate decision.
judgment.recommended_action: Request only elevation/install-scope status and one same-session comparison, then reclassify based on whether the failure is limited to elevated Terminal or remains in non-elevated Terminal and other apps.

fix_assessment.rationale: No code fix is supportable until elevation and cross-application evidence rule out a UIPI/integrity-level boundary or other Terminal-specific behavior. This is a no-design disposition pending the targeted answer, not a claim that Keyboard Manager cannot be responsible.

issue_context.summary: A specific Caps Lock-to-Esc remap is reportedly ignored in Windows Terminal, including a WSL2 session, but the report does not say whether Terminal is elevated or whether the same remap fails outside Terminal.
known_information: PowerToys 0.102.2814; Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0; PowerShell 7.4.6 or WSL2 2.7.3.0 with Ubuntu 24.04.5; nvim in WSL2.
The configured remap is Caps Lock to Esc; the reporter expects Esc and reports that Caps Lock is triggered instead.
No diagnostic archive or author follow-up is present. Automated triage lists #28728 as a possible duplicate.
inferences: If Windows Terminal is elevated while PowerToys is not, UIPI may block synthetic input; the current evidence does not establish this.
If the remap fails only in non-elevated Windows Terminal but succeeds in Notepad, a Terminal-specific input path is more likely; neither comparison is reported.
issue_context.analysis: The previous #28728 report described the same Terminal symptom and a maintainer asked whether Terminal was running as administrator; that issue was later closed after no author answer, so it supplies a useful discriminator but no fix. Current Keyboard Manager code uses a SendVirtualInput abstraction and explicitly accounts for injection being blocked by UIPI in a remap path. Ask for the two narrow facts before proposing a competing design.
initial_investigation: At upstream source head 1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a, KeyboardManager InputInterface::SendVirtualInput abstracts synthetic input; KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp includes handling/comments for injection blocked by UIPI. This supports checking integrity levels but does not prove that the reported remap fails for that reason.

Read the complete linked #28728 issue: it reports remapping failing in Windows Terminal but working in Chrome/Edge; a maintainer asked whether Terminal ran as administrator, and the issue later closed as stale with no response or documented fix: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/28728.
No exact #51303 issue, PR, or branch trace was found in MuyuanMS/PowerToys.

information_gaps.information: Whether PowerToys and Windows Terminal are elevated, and whether they run in the same Windows user session.
information_gaps.why_needed: A higher-integrity Terminal can reject injected input from a non-elevated PowerToys process; this changes whether a code fix is applicable.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: In Task Manager > Details, enable the Elevated column and report Yes/No for both PowerToys and Windows Terminal; state whether both use the same Windows user. No screenshot is needed.

information_gaps.information: Whether Caps Lock-to-Esc works in Notepad in the same session and whether it still fails in a non-elevated Windows Terminal.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates an application-specific Terminal path from a general Keyboard Manager remapping/injection failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: With the same PowerToys configuration, test the remap in Notepad and in a non-elevated Windows Terminal, then report each result.

actions.label: Confirm Terminal elevation and remap behavior

comment.body:
Thanks for the exact Caps Lock-to-Esc mapping and the Windows Terminal, PowerShell, and WSL versions. One key distinction is not in the report yet: whether the Terminal process is elevated, and whether the same mapping works in another app.

Please provide:
1. Whether PowerToys and Windows Terminal are elevated and whether they run under the same Windows user. In Task Manager > Details, enable the Elevated column and report Yes or No for each.
2. Whether Caps Lock-to-Esc works in Notepad in the same session; if possible, also test a non-elevated Windows Terminal.

This will distinguish an OS integrity-level input-injection boundary from a Terminal-specific input path and determine whether a Keyboard Manager code change is indicated.
